nodes.description: Loss of functional Complex IV blocks terminal electron transfer from cytochrome c to molecular oxygen and proton pumping across the inner mitochondrial membrane, collapsing oxidative ATP synthesis and accompanied by marked cellular copper deficiency due to loss of SCO1-mediated copper homeostasis. In mammals, SCO1 is expressed at ~15-fold higher levels than SCO2 in liver (and strongly in vascular endothelial cells), explaining the predilection of severe SCO1 deficiency for liver, brain, endocrine, and cardiac tissues, with residual allelic capacity shaping phenotypic severity.
